card.hook: Squint a little and you could be in Windsor, not South Bohemia. Hluboká Castle looks more English than Czech, and that's half its charm.
card.stand_here: Head to the spot near Bezručova, about 85 m west of the castle (the phone icon on the map), and face east. The castle is about 134 m away, roughly 2 minutes on foot.
card.zoom: Start at 1x to get the whole front with its battlements and pale stonework against the sky. Then try 2x for towers and rooflines. Use 0.5x only if you want trees or a path in the foreground, because the castle will look smaller and a bit stretched near the edges.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and line the towers up with the vertical lines so they don't lean.
card.best_time: Pick a dry day, and go when it's quieter if you can. From here you face east, so the morning sun may be behind the castle and a later visit might suit the front better.
card.selfie_here: Try the small pond in the castle grounds, which one guide says reflects the towers, and turn so the towers are behind you (sunrise is the time sources suggest). Use the front camera at 0.5x, hold it a bit low, and check on your screen that the towers are over your shoulder. The terraces of the formal gardens on the south side are another good setting.
card.ask_someone: For a shot of the castle with the garden in the foreground, ask a passer-by to take it from the top of the hill opposite the castle.
card.rules_and_safety: You can photograph the outside, courtyards and gardens freely without a tour ticket, but photos are forbidden inside the castle during tours. Drones aren't allowed in the grounds, and watch out for ticks in the gardens.
card.challenge: Get all the towers standing straight against the grid, with a tree branch in one corner and not a single stranger's head in the shot.
card.good_to_know: A Gothic castle stood here from the second half of the 13th century, and it was later reworked in Renaissance and Baroque styles. Today's look comes from a rebuild between 1841 and 1871 in the romantic style of Windsor Castle. The English-style park around it covers roughly 1.9 square kilometres, so there's plenty of greenery to frame your shot.

card.hook: Here's a zoo trick: you can photograph a wolf-dog's cousins in the morning and a fairy-tale chateau in the same frame, without turning around. Ohrada's pond does all the work.
card.stand_here: Stand right at the subject, on the pond side of the zoo on the south shore of the Munický rybník. Face across the water: Hluboká chateau sits on the horizon, with the pond in front of it.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to get the pond, sky, chateau and shoreline all in one go. Then try 1x for a more natural look, and 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) to pull the chateau closer or snap animals from a distance.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the chateau, then drag the brightness slider down a touch (darker) so the sky keeps its colour.
card.best_time: There's no single best time here. Check the zoo's opening hours before you plan your visit.
card.selfie_here: Try the pier on the pond bank next to the little refreshment-stand garden: the zoo area and the castle across the pond can be seen together from there. Use the front camera at 0.5x and keep the castle over your shoulder. The wooden footbridges inside the zoo are another option, with an open view over the pond. Check on site which way the castle backdrop falls.
card.ask_someone: On the forecourt in front of the Ohrada hunting lodge's main façade, on the walk from the car park to the zoo gate, ask someone to take a photo of you with the lodge behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: Entry to both the zoo and the chateau may be ticketed, so check the official sites before you go.
card.challenge: Take one wide shot with the pond and chateau, then one close-up of an animal's eye, and see if they look like they came from the same trip.
card.good_to_know: Ohrada Zoo (also called Zoo Hluboká) opened in 1939 and keeps mainly animals from Europe and the Czech Republic, so the enclosures feel local rather than exotic. It has a place in dog history too: in 1983 its wolf Lejdy gave birth to the last line of what became the Czechoslovakian Wolfdog breed. The chateau also looks back across the pond towards the Ohrada hunting lodge, but that's a distance shot of the lodge, not the zoo.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found gives a selfie stick or tripod rule, so none is listed. The pier and footbridge spots come from secondary blogs and galleries, not an official zoo map, so the exact spots and the direction of the castle backdrop should be checked on site. The ask-someone spot is the lodge façade by the zoo approach, which is a named part of the complex but not the zoo gate itself; no page names a place with the whole zoo in one frame. The zoo's Christmas lit-up event had named photo spots, but it ran only 28 Nov 2025 to 4 Jan 2026, so it is not current. The coordinates in the zoo's own listing differ slightly from the position you gave, and the zoo's own site does not name any photo spot.

card.hook: Statues don't mind if you walk circles around them, and that's your best trick here. One side will have a much cleaner background than the others, so take a lap before you press the button.
card.stand_here: The Waldemar statue is about 154 metres west of the stand-here point on the map, so face west and walk toward it. Take one wide shot as you approach, then move closer.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x, a few steps back, with the phone upright so the whole figure and its base fit in. Go to 2x-5x for details like the face or the base (higher zooms depend on your phone), and use 0.5x only if you can stand close and want lots of the setting.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on the gridlines to keep the statue straight, and if the sky behind is bright, tap the statue and drag the slider so the picture gets a little darker, so the figure doesn't turn into a dark shape.
card.best_time: Soft morning or late-afternoon light flatters statues most. Overcast days work well too, because the light is nice and even.
card.selfie_here: Use the front camera, switch to 0.5x if your phone has it, and hold the phone a bit higher with the statue behind your shoulder. Step a metre or two sideways first, so signs, bins and parked cars stay out of the background.
card.rules_and_safety: We don't know the access rules for this spot, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Take two shots of the statue, one wide with the whole base and a bit of space above the head, and one close-up of the face. Then pick your favourite.
card.good_to_know: The Waldemar statue is the third spot on this map. We don't have any history, dates or size for it, so look for an information board nearby if you want the background story.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a 'Waldemar' statue in Hluboká nad Vltavou, so I could not identify a selfie spot or a photographer spot for it, and I did not add any place from memory. The searches returned general castle pages: Atlas Obscura (https://www.atlasobscura.com/places/the-state-chateau-of-hluboka) gives the castle coordinates as 49.051124, 14.441594, close to your position, and the castle's own site (https://www.hluboka.cz/en/activities/51-statni-zamek-hluboka-nad-vltavou) lists the castle park as a visitable area. Neither mentions a Waldemar statue. A Czech page (https://zamekhluboka.info/prohlidky/) mentions other sculptures in the park, but none named Waldemar. Please check the exact spelling or the statue's location (for example, a park sculpture or a statue in the town) before relying on this. No page I found gave any selfie-stick or tripod rules, so I have none to report.
